title: Submodularity of entropy under quantum convolution
abstract: We develop a submodular framework for the von Neumann entropy of discrete quantum convolutions, providing a noncommutative counterpart to the direct side of entropic additive combinatorics. We first introduce globally weighted quantum convolutions, which form compatible families indexed by admissible subsets of a fixed collection of inputs. Our main theorem reveals a polymatroidal geometry underlying their entropy growth: relative to any fixed admissible input block, the entropy gains admit a normalized, monotone, submodular extension to all subsets of the remaining inputs. The theorem yields convolutional strong subadditivity, quantum Ruzsa triangle inequality, and quantum entropic Plünnecke--Ruzsa inequalities for arbitrary input states. For repeated inputs, it gives sharp comparisons of entropy growth across admissible scales; in particular, the quantum doubling constant controls all higher admissible convolution entropies with optimal exponents. Together, these results bring submodular methods from additive combinatorics into the quantum setting and provide a systematic route to broad families of convolutional entropy inequalities.
summary: This paper establishes a deep mathematical structure—submodularity—for the von Neumann entropy associated with quantum convolutions. By developing a framework using characteristic kernels, the authors prove fundamental inequalities, such as the quantum Ruzsa triangle inequality, which generalize classical results from additive combinatorics into the quantum realm.
main_problem: The paper develops a submodular framework for the von Neumann entropy associated with discrete quantum convolutions, aiming to provide a noncommutative analogue to entropic additive combinatorics.
main_result: The entropy gains of quantum convolutions are governed by a polymatroidal geometry, leading to proofs of convolutional strong subadditivity and the quantum Ruzsa triangle inequality.
method: The authors utilize characteristic-kernel methods and establish submodularity by relating the entropy function to the marginals of an auxiliary separable state, leveraging strong subadditivity.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum states ($ho$) on $n$-qudit systems defined over a discrete phase space $V_n = \mathbb{Z}_d^n 	imes \mathbb{Z}_d^n$, analyzing the entropy of quantum convolutions ($ho  oxtimes \sigma$).
key_observables: Von Neumann entropy ($S$), entropy gain function ($J(\cdot)$), quantum Ruzsa divergence ($D_{Rz}$), and the quantum doubling constant ($\delta_q$).
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ (an odd prime), the size of the system $n$, and the structure of admissible subsets.
main_assumptions: The results are primarily restricted to globally weighted quantum convolutions forming compatible families, and the proofs rely on the existence of an auxiliary separable state $\Omega$.
figures_summary: Not specified by the notes, but the structure implies derivations of inequalities (e.g., 4.6, 5.10) and the definition of various divergence measures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the quantum convolution via characteristic kernels, then establishing the submodular structure of the entropy gain function (Theorem 4.1), and finally applying this structure to derive major inequalities like strong subadditivity and the Ruzsa triangle inequality.
why_interesting: The connection between submodularity (a powerful tool from combinatorics) and fundamental quantum information measures like entropy provides deep structural insights into how quantum correlations grow under convolution operations.
